title: Manakish cheese
subtitle: Lebanese flatbread with melted akkawi and nigella seeds
excerpt: Manakish (or mana'eesh) are Lebanese flatbreads baked to order at street bakeries across the Levant. The cheese version is topped with akkawi or nabulsi, a salty white cheese that melts into a golden, lightly stringy topping scattered with nigella seeds. They are morning food: eaten fresh from the oven wrapped in paper.
sourceNotes: Manakish are the most common street breakfast food across Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, and Palestine. They are baked in a traditional flat oven (taboun) but work well in a very hot domestic oven or on a cast-iron griddle.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can be made the evening before and cold-proved overnight. Shape and bake fresh.
recipe.temperatureNote: Preheat fully for 30 minutes; place on the top shelf

content.text: Manakish cheese are exactly what they sound like: hot flatbreads covered in melted cheese. But the cheese matters. Akkawi or nabulsi are brined white cheeses that melt without becoming greasy and that have a mild, milky saltiness unlike any western cheese. If you cannot find them, halloumi grated coarsely is the closest substitute.

Manakish are morning food. In Lebanon, people stop at the mana'eesh stand on the way to work and eat them wrapped in paper with fresh tomato and fresh mint. Making them at home requires a very hot oven and a light hand with the dough.
The dough is a straightforward yeasted flatbread dough that can be made the night before.

items.prepNote: or akkawi/nabulsi if available, crumbled or coarsely grated

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, and sugar together. Add the oil and warm water and mix to a dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and slightly elastic. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and leave to rise for 45 to 60 minutes until doubled.

Preheat the oven to 250 C. Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each into a thin round about 20 cm across; they should be no thicker than 4 mm. Place on a lightly oiled baking sheet. Mix the crumbled feta and grated mozzarella together. Spread the cheese mixture over each round, leaving a 1 cm border. Scatter with nigella seeds and drizzle a little olive oil over each.

Bake on the top shelf for 8 to 10 minutes until the edges are golden and the cheese is melted and patchy with colour. Serve immediately; manakish go soft quickly and are best eaten straight from the oven.

rows.cause: Dough resisting rolling from too much spring
rows.fix: Let each piece rest for 5 minutes after the first attempt, then roll again; the gluten will have relaxed.

rows.cause: Excess moisture in feta or mozzarella
rows.fix: Press feta dry in kitchen paper before using. Pat mozzarella dry too.

rows.cause: Oven not hot enough or cheese too wet
rows.fix: The oven must be very hot. Preheat for at least 30 minutes before baking.

content.text: The classic alternative to cheese manakish is zaatar (dried herb and sesame paste). Make a paste from 2 tbsp zaatar spice blend, 1 tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of sumac and spread it instead of the cheese. Both versions are served with sliced tomato, cucumber, and fresh mint.
The dough keeps overnight in the fridge after its first rise. Shape and bake fresh. Baked manakish do not store well; they are morning food and best eaten within minutes of baking.

Manakish are the street breakfast of the Levant. In Beirut, Amman, and Damascus, small bakeries open early and sell hundreds of manakish through the morning. They are eaten on the street, in cars, and at kitchen tables. The cheese version and the zaatar version are the two most common.
